back: Loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant: evaporation from mesophyll cell walls, then diffusion of vapour out through stomata.

front: Volume of water taken up in a potometer
back: V = πr²l (r = capillary radius, l = distance moved by the bubble).
Evaporation from leaves → tension in xylem → cohesion (hydrogen bonds) pulls the column up → adhesion to walls helps.
Higher light intensity, higher temperature, more wind, lower humidity.

front: Why cut a shoot under water for a potometer?
back: To stop air entering the xylem and breaking the water column.
Rolled leaf, sunken stomata in grooves, hairs, thick cuticle on the outer surface, stomata only on the inner surface.

front: Evidence that xylem sap is under tension
back: Trunk diameter shrinks when transpiration is fastest; cut vessels draw air in.
Attraction of water molecules to the hydrophilic walls of xylem vessels by hydrogen bonding.
Removes humid air around the leaf, keeping a steep water vapour potential gradient.
